chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'May I not be the first of the four witnesses upon the adulterer, for fear that one of them might withdraw, so I would be whipped.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali avoid being the first witness in adultery cases?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) narrates that he deliberately avoided being the first of the four required witnesses in a case of adultery (zina) to protect himself from the punishment of flogging (jald) if any of the other witnesses were to withdraw their testimony. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the strict evidentiary standards for hadd punishments, where the withdrawal of even one witness invalidates the case, thereby exposing the remaining three to the penalty of false testimony. The incident highlights the practical application of legal caution (ihtiyat) by the Imams in ensuring justice and avoiding premature punishment.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>:
‘Amir Al Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May I<sup>asws</sup> not be the first of the witnessed upon the adultery, for fear that one of them might withdraw, so I<sup>asws</sup> would be whipped’.
